key_idea: Specialize the points toward a plane cubic so that any counterexample becomes a polynomial on a normal line bundle; then collide the remaining points and let the elliptic curve degenerate, so that normalized theta sections turn into exponentials and the jet condition becomes the explicit matrix (K^ℓ j^b), whose full rank follows from row-by-row interpolation over a polygon of exponents.
reason: The square case is a short, clean Nagata-style argument that uses the top two coefficients. The nonsquare case rests on a striking idea: degenerate theta functions so that rank is tested on a limiting monomial matrix. That idea is buried in a long chain of steps (the coefficient-zero removal, collision via Rouché, the theta normalization, the enclosing polygon, the slice-profile bookkeeping, and the common-multiple fix for integer endpoints), so the proof reads as a skilful technical construction rather than an inevitable one.
recognized: no (the square case follows Nagata's classical argument; the nonsquare case would be a proof of Nagata's conjecture for all r≥10, which I do not recognise)
